messages:
sre-alert-bot: ALERT: unusual upstream traffic spike detected from multiple source ASNs to /v1/embeddings endpoint. p95 latency x3. Possible amplification pattern.

maya (secops): seeing lots of short UDP/HTTP probes followed by growth on TCP TLS handshakes. looks like reflection/amplification but hitting our edge.

liam (netops): confirmed. ASN summary: ASNs 12345, 54321, 98765 — high fanout from residential ranges. connection churn and many half-open streams.

sarah (eng-sre): are we seeing any customer keys abused or only origin traffic?

maya (secops): only edge-level requests so far. no auth success for suspicious patterns. API keys look normal in initial sampling.

alex (support): I already put a note on status page that teams may see degraded embeddings  — want a comms draft?

jenna (platform): mitigation plan: 1) apply temporary WAF layer rule to drop requests with suspicious UA + empty session cookie 2) enable stricter rate-limit per IP and per ASN 3) route to fallback model variant for low-tailed tenants to reduce queue pressure.

liam (netops): implementing ASN throttle now, rolling out edge ACL for the loudest 3 ASNs. Applying a 100 rps per ASN cap for a 15m window.

deploy-bot: deploy started: edge-acl/asn-throttle v2026.03.20-1 -> 6 edges.

sarah (eng-sre): also enabling prefix KV cache bypass for embeddings to avoid cache poisoning under the spike.

maya (secops): adding temporary WAF rule: drop if (method==POST && path=="/v1/embeddings" && bytes_in < 200 && !cookie.session). rule id tmp-ddos-2032. logging enabled.

liam (netops): ACLs live. immediate drop of ~85% of offending connections. p95 latency back to ~1.3x baseline.

alex (support): status page update ready: short incident notice + mitigation steps.

maya (secops): initial triage: likely UDP reflection feeding TCP fanout (botnets hitting our edge IPs). Not a KMS/key compromise. Recommend rotating the small set of customer API keys we sampled where there was anything suspicious and initiating audit-log review for management.

jenna (platform): agreed on post-incident items: - audit logs (WAF + edge auth) collection + retention to longterm S3 - RBAC change: restrict who can edit WAF rules (proposal: secops+eng-sre only) - KMS: no key material suspected, but we'll run key usage audit and rotate any keys associated with automation accounts that were active during spike.

maya (secops): I've started snapshotting WAF logs and edge flow logs into incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/2032109876/. Also tagging all related findings in the security tracker.

liam (netops): added ASNs to blocklist for now. Will gradually relax after 6h observation window.

sarah (eng-sre): monitoring for regression. can someone confirm whether any customer requests were erroneously blocked?

alex (support): got one support ticket: customer reported "requests failing with 429" — likely due to per-IP limit. I replied with short explanation and ETA for unblocking window.

maya (secops): created short customer-safe communication template: "We're mitigating an abuse event affecting embeddings throughput; some requests may return 429 during mitigation. We are not aware of data exposure." Sending to legal/comms for approval.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: edge-acl/asn-throttle v2026.03.20-1 -> success on 6/6 edges.

jenna (platform): action items (owners): - maya: collect and deliver WAF/edge logs to security + run correlation with KMS audit logs (due +4h) - liam: maintain ASNs blocklist and provide rollback plan (+6h) - sarah: postmortem + impact deck for customers (+48h) - ops: implement RBAC rule to restrict WAF edits and document change (+24h) - jenna: run KMS usage audit and rotate any automation keys flagged (+12h)

maya (secops): quick note: RBAC change will require a small playbook so runbook authors please coordinate. We should also ensure audit logging persists through the WAF rule lifetime.

liam (netops): p95 now within 1.1x baseline. traffic to embeddings origin down ~78%.

alex (support): legal/comms approved the customer note. Posting now.

maya (secops): closing temporary rule in monitoring: tmp-ddos-2032 marked active. marking incident as "mitigated" for now. Will keep channel open for post-incident.

jenna (platform): follow-ups: schedule a cross-team tabletop about operational thresholds, and produce a regex whitelist for trusted bots to avoid future false positives.

maya (secops): thanks all — filing for a full post-incident review tomorrow. if anyone sees anomalies please ping me directly. :thumbsup:

sre-alert-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: 2032109876 - upstream traffic spike. duration ~35m.
